name: Colombo
tagline: Sri Lanka's seafront capital, colonial bones and Indian Ocean spice.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: December to March is dry and clear on the west coast, with Galle's literary festival in January; avoid the May–September southwest monsoon.

ourTake.lede: Colombo has quietly become worth a stay in its own right rather than just an airport you pass through on the way to the beaches or the hill country. Give it a day and a half: the Dutch-era Fort and Pettah for the mornings, Galle Face Green at dusk with the kite-sellers and isso wade, and dinner in one of the restored Cinnamon Gardens bungalows. Don't overplan it; the pleasure here is walking a compact, humid, layered city and eating extremely well.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a short, low-effort island break with colonial-era streets, sea air and unhurried days a couple of hours from home.
ourTake.skipIf: You are chasing dramatic landscapes or a marquee destination, Colombo is a gateway city, not the headline.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Shangri-La Colombo
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Hotel 2024
World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Hotel 2023 & 2022
items.description: The most decorated address in the city, standing where the ocean meets the old capital.

items.name: ITC Ratnadipa, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Conference Hotel 2025
Marriott Luxury Collection
Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority 5-Star Classification
LEED Platinum (US Green Building Council, 2024)
items.description: The city's newest icon, a twin-tower waterfront house from a group that knows the Indian traveller by name.

items.name: The Kingsbury Colombo
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Hotel 2025
items.description: An art-deco landmark between Galle Face Green and the harbour, lately crowned the island's finest.

items.name: Cinnamon Grand Colombo
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Business Hotel 2024
items.description: The city's grand social house, where Colombo comes to dine, marry and be seen.

items.name: Cinnamon Lakeside Colombo
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Hotel nominee 2024, 2025 & 2026
Best Five-Star City Hotel, Sri Lanka Tourism
items.description: A calm lakeside house away from the traffic, with the water for a garden.

items.name: Amari Colombo
credentials: World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Business Hotel 2025
items.description: A crisp, contemporary seafront house that runs like clockwork for the working traveller.

items.name: Galle Face Hotel
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2024, No. 1, Best Hotels in Asia (Rest of Asia)
Best Heritage Hotel, Sri Lanka Tourism Awards 2024
items.description: One of the oldest hotels east of Suez, 1864 colonial grandeur, still keeping the sea at its feet.

items.name: Galle Face Green at sunset
items.description: A kilometre of ocean-facing lawn that has been Colombo's front garden since Victorian times, where at golden hour the whole city comes out to fly kites, walk the seawall and watch the sun drop into the Indian Ocean. Street carts sell isso wade (shrimp fritters), kottu and hoppers to the spice-loving subcontinental palate. A private driver drops the family at the seawall and waits while grandparents and children share the same easy, unhurried ritual.

items.name: Galle Face Hotel
items.description: The Grande Dame of South Asia, open since 1864 and the only hotel in Colombo with genuine beachfront, its checkerboard verandah and lantern-lit lawn a stage for a century and a half of royalty and film stars. Come for high tea, a Ceylon-arrack sundowner as the doorman lights the evening lamps, or a heritage-wing suite. Won Best Heritage Hotel at the Sri Lanka Tourism Awards and a discreet, colonial-glamour anchor for any Colombo stay.

items.name: Gangaramaya Temple
items.description: One of Colombo's most important and eclectic Buddhist temples, a treasure-house of Buddha images, vintage cars, ivory, jade and gifts from devotees packed into a working monastery beside Beira Lake. The famous February Navam Perahera procession of elephants and dancers starts here. For an Indian family the shared Buddhist-Hindu iconography and the calm of the shrine make it instantly legible; a monk-guided visit deepens it.

items.name: Seema Malaka
items.description: Geoffrey Bawa's serene meditation pavilion, three timber-and-blue-tile platforms that appear to float on Beira Lake, rebuilt in 1976 after the original sank. Rows of seated Buddha statues face the water in the middle of the city, and the whole thing is a masterclass in Bawa's tropical modernism. Quietest at dawn or dusk; a five-minute stop from Gangaramaya and one of the most photographed calm spaces in Colombo.

items.name: Colombo Fort colonial quarter
items.description: The colonial heart of the capital, once a Portuguese-then-Dutch-then-British fort and now a grid of grand facades, banks and old trading houses along the harbour. Walk it with a heritage guide to read the Neo-Renaissance and Victorian stonework layer by layer. Compact, atmospheric and best in the cool of early morning before the commercial bustle takes over.

items.name: Old Dutch Hospital precinct
items.description: Believed to be the oldest building in the Fort, dating to Dutch rule around 1681, its thick-walled courtyards restored in 2011 into Colombo's most elegant dining-and-shopping precinct. Ministry of Crab and smart boutiques now fill the colonnades. An easy, air-conditioned, veg-friendly place for a multi-generational lunch that still feels three centuries old.

items.name: Cargills & Millers building
items.description: A grand red-brick department-store facade from 1906, all arched windows and ornate ironwork, one of the finest surviving pieces of Victorian commercial architecture in the city and the home of Sri Lanka's oldest retailer. A striking photo stop on any Fort walk and a window into Ceylon's trading heyday.

items.name: Colombo Lighthouse Clock Tower
items.description: Built in 1857 with its clock added in 1860, this is believed to be the only structure in the world that served as both a working lighthouse and a clock tower in the middle of a capital city, and the original mechanism still runs. A quick, charming landmark at the centre of the Fort's colonial streetscape.

items.name: Pettah bazaar
items.description: Colombo's oldest and most frantic market district, block after block of wholesale produce, gold and jewellery streets, textiles, spices and electronics spilling across the pavements. It is the raw, sensory heart of the city, immediately familiar to anyone who knows an Indian bazaar. Go with a guide or on a food tour to move through it with ease.

items.name: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque (the Red Mosque)
items.description: The candy-striped red-and-white 1908 mosque whose pomegranate-shaped domes once guided sailors to Colombo's shore before modern navigation. Its Indo-Saracenic exterior is one of the most photographed facades in the country. Visitors may see the interior outside prayer times with modest dress; a five-minute walk from the Pettah stalls.

items.name: Wolvendaal Church
items.description: Sri Lanka's oldest Protestant church, a cross-shaped Dutch Reformed building in use since 1749, its floor paved with the tombstones of Dutch governors and an 18th-century carved pulpit still in place. A hushed, deeply atmospheric survivor of colonial Colombo, minutes from the chaos of Pettah.

items.name: Colombo National Museum
items.description: The island's premier museum, founded in 1877 in a gleaming white colonial building, home to the regalia and gem-set throne of the last Kandyan kings, ancient bronzes, masks and a sweep of Sri Lankan civilisation. The single best primer before heading to the cultural triangle. Cool, calm and rewarding for curious teenagers and grandparents alike.

items.name: Independence Memorial Hall & the Arcade
items.description: The open-sided monument to Ceylon's 1948 independence, modelled on the royal audience hall of the Kandyan kings with rows of carved stone pillars and guardian lions, set on a grand ceremonial square. The adjoining Arcade Independence Square, a restored colonial asylum-turned-mall, brings smart boutiques and cafes for a relaxed browse. Evenings are cool and photogenic.

items.name: Viharamahadevi Park
items.description: Colombo's largest green space, 50 acres of flowering trees, lakes and a golden Buddha statue laid out beside the National Museum. It bursts into bloom with flamboyant orange blossoms in season and is a gentle, shaded place for a morning stroll with children before the heat. A calm counterpoint to the city's traffic.

items.name: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
items.description: A temple with more than 2,500 years of history, believed to have been hallowed by the Buddha's third visit to the island, its walls covered in the celebrated Solias Mendis murals of Buddhist history and Jataka tales beneath a great white stupa. Only a short drive from the city and profoundly moving for a Buddhist or Hindu family; the reclining Buddha and lotus offerings feel entirely at home.

items.name: Colombo Lotus Tower
items.description: At 350 metres the tallest self-supported structure in South Asia, its rosy petals lighting up over the skyline at night. Ride to the observation deck for a 360-degree view of the city and coast, then the revolving restaurant above it. A fun, family-pleasing hour and the clearest way to grasp Colombo's layout.

items.name: Number 11, Geoffrey Bawa's house
items.description: The intimate city home of the father of tropical modernism, a set of knocked-through row houses turned into a jewel-box of courtyards, art, white light and greenery, kept exactly as Bawa left it. Visitable only by the Trust's guided tour, with two suites now bookable for a night inside the master's own rooms. Essential for anyone who loves design and the maker behind Amangalla and the Bawa hotels.

items.name: Paradise Road The Gallery Café
items.description: Set in Geoffrey Bawa's former design office, an all-white courtyard restaurant that is Colombo's most stylish lunch and one of the city's design landmarks. Contemporary Sri Lankan and Continental plates, a famous chocolate-fudge dessert and an adjoining gallery of local art. Reserve ahead; an elegant, veg-friendly pause between sights.

items.name: Barefoot Garden Café & Gallery
items.description: The leafy courtyard cafe behind Barefoot, the beloved handloom and design store founded by artist Barbara Sansoni, famous for its jewel-toned striped textiles, bookshop, gallery and Sunday live jazz. A relaxed, creative afternoon and the best place to buy genuinely good Sri Lankan design and gifts.

items.name: Paradise Road flagship store
items.description: The mother ship of Sri Lankan design retail, a beautiful colonial house filled with covetable homeware, ceramics, linens and gifts in the label's signature restrained aesthetic. The most refined souvenir shopping in the city and a natural stop for design-minded travellers.

items.name: Ministry of Crab
items.description: Widely called Colombo's best restaurant, co-founded by cricket legends Mahela Jayawardene and Kumar Sangakkara, serving giant Sri Lankan lagoon crab in garlic, chilli and pepper inside the 17th-century Dutch Hospital. A bucket-list table for seafood lovers; book weeks ahead. Not one for a strictly vegetarian party, but a highlight for the rest.

items.name: Tuk-tuk street-food tour of Colombo
items.description: The most fun way to eat the city, weaving by tuk-tuk between Pettah stalls, hopper carts and hidden eateries for kottu roti, string hoppers, isso wade and Ceylon tea. Guides tailor the route for vegetarian and Jain families, and the shared subcontinental spice palate means very little needs translating. A joyful, low-key evening for all ages.

items.name: Mount Lavinia beach & hotel
items.description: The nearest proper beach to the city, named for a governor's love story, with the grand colonial Mount Lavinia Hotel on the headland above golden sand and a long line of seafood restaurants along the shore. Come for a lazy beach lunch, a swim and a sundowner on the terrace where the British once danced. An easy half-day escape from the capital.

items.name: Beira Lake
items.description: The city's calm inner lake, its shore cradling Seema Malaka and Gangaramaya and its water dotted with swan pedal-boats at Nawaloka. A gentle, green pause in the middle of the traffic, loveliest at dusk when the temple lights reflect on the surface.

items.name: Nelum Pokuna Theatre
items.description: Colombo's grand performing-arts theatre, its form modelled on the ancient lotus pond at Polonnaruwa, staging Kandyan dance, classical music, ballet and concerts. Check the calendar for a night of traditional drumming and dance, a graceful and family-friendly cultural evening in the city.

items.name: Cricket at the SSC or P Sara Oval
items.description: The Sinhalese Sports Club ground is the spiritual home of Sri Lankan cricket, while the historic P Sara Oval hosted the island's first Test match. For a cricket-mad Indian family, a Test or club match here, tea and short-eats in hand, is pure joy. A private box or club access turns it into an occasion.

items.name: Colombo Racecourse & Cinnamon Gardens stroll
items.description: The 1893 colonial racecourse, its grandstand now a smart dining-and-shopping arcade, sits amid Cinnamon Gardens, the city's leafiest and most gracious quarter of embassies, mansions and rugby pitches. A pleasant afternoon of coffee, a wander past the colonial villas and a sense of old, moneyed Colombo.

items.name: Kandy & the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (day trip / overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Sacred City of Kandy
items.description: The last royal capital of the Sinhalese kings, cradled in misty hills around a lake, home to the golden shrine that holds the Buddha's tooth relic and the nightly drumming ritual around it. Best as an overnight with a private guide and driver; the evening Kandyan dance and the Peradeniya gardens fill out the day. Profoundly resonant for a Buddhist or Hindu family.

items.name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress (day trip / overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Ancient City of Sigiriya
items.description: A 200-metre column of rock crowned with a 5th-century sky palace, reached past the famous cloud-maiden frescoes and a colossal lion's-paw gateway, with water gardens laid out below. One of Asia's great climbs and views; go at dawn to beat the heat and the crowds. Best paired with a night at a nearby luxury lodge rather than rushed from Colombo.

items.name: Dambulla Cave Temple (Golden Temple)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Golden Temple of Dambulla
items.description: Five ancient caves cut into a rock massif, holding over 150 Buddha statues and a ceiling of exquisite murals dating back to the 1st century BC, the best-preserved cave-temple complex on the island. Usually combined with Sigiriya, a short drive away, into one unforgettable cultural-triangle day.

items.name: Galle Fort & Amangalla (overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications
items.description: The best-preserved colonial sea-fort in Asia, a walkable warren of Dutch mansions, boutiques, cafes and ramparts you circle at sunset. Stay inside the walls at Amangalla, a 17th-century building and one of the world's finest hotels, for the full discreet-luxury experience. Reachable by the coastal expressway in two hours; deserves at least a night.

items.name: Bentota, Lunuganga & Brief Garden
items.description: A palm-lined river-and-beach town that is the cradle of Bawa design, home to Lunuganga, Geoffrey Bawa's 15-acre garden estate and lifelong masterpiece, and nearby Brief Garden, the wilder, art-filled retreat of his brother Bevis. A day among Sri Lanka's most beautiful private landscapes, ideally with a night in a Bawa-designed villa on the coast.

items.name: Yala National Park leopard safari (multi-day)
items.description: One of the best places on earth to see a wild leopard, with among the highest densities anywhere, plus elephants, sloth bears and lagoon birdlife. Stay at a luxury tented camp like Leopard Trails and take private dawn game drives. A proper multi-day trip, and the wildlife highlight of any Sri Lankan itinerary.

items.name: Wilpattu National Park (multi-day)
items.description: The island's largest and wildest national park, quieter than Yala, dotted with natural lakes (villus) and good for leopard, elephant and sloth bear in a more solitary setting. The nearer northern alternative for a family that wants big-game safari without the crowds, paired with a luxury camp.

items.name: Ella & the hill-country tea trains (multi-day)
items.description: The misty tea highlands reached on one of the world's most beautiful rail journeys, past emerald plantations, waterfalls and the Nine Arch Bridge. Stay in a restored planter's bungalow with the Ceylon Tea Trails, walk a working estate and take tea where it is grown. A slow, cool, romantic contrast to the coast, best over several days.

items.name: Anuradhapura, the ancient sacred city (overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Sacred City of Anuradhapura
items.description: Sri Lanka's first great capital, a vast spread of colossal brick dagobas, monastic ruins and the Sri Maha Bodhi, grown from a cutting of the tree under which the Buddha found enlightenment and among the oldest living planted trees on earth. Deeply sacred and best explored by bicycle or car with a guide. An overnight from Colombo or part of a cultural-triangle loop.

items.name: Polonnaruwa, the medieval capital (overnight)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Ancient City of Polonnaruwa
items.description: The island's superbly preserved 11th-12th century royal city, its highlight the Gal Vihara group of giant granite Buddhas carved from a single rock face. Compact enough to cycle in a morning and richly rewarding. Usually combined with Sigiriya and Dambulla into a cultural-triangle stay rather than a Colombo day trip.

items.name: Negombo & the Ramayana trail
items.description: The fishing town beside the airport, threaded with Dutch canals and a lively morning fish market, and a stop on Sri Lanka's Ramayana pilgrimage circuit. For Hindu families following the Sita story, nearby Munneswaram temple and the wider trail of Ashok Vatika and Divurumpola give the island a second, devotional layer beyond its Buddhist heart.

items.name: Sri Lankan spa & Ayurveda ritual
items.description: The island's living Ayurvedic tradition, shared with India, is offered at the finest level in Colombo's hotel spas and at retreats down the coast, from herbal oil treatments to full multi-day panchakarma programmes. A restorative half-day for a multi-generational group between sightseeing, in familiar hands.

items.name: Gem & jewellery house visit
items.description: Ceylon has been the source of the world's finest blue sapphires for two thousand years, and Colombo's established jewellers and gem houses offer private appointments to see certified stones and commission pieces. For a family with a connoisseur's eye it is a genuine, discreet luxury the island does better than almost anywhere.

items.name: Dutch Period Museum
items.description: The 17th-century former townhouse of a Dutch governor, now a small museum of colonial furniture, coins and artefacts around a shaded courtyard. A quiet, cool retreat in the middle of Pettah and a fine complement to Wolvendaal Church for anyone chasing the Dutch story.

items.name: Old Parliament & the Presidential Secretariat waterfront
items.description: The stately colonnaded former parliament building on Galle Face, all white neoclassical grandeur facing the sea, one of the handsomest colonial set-pieces in the city. Admire it from the promenade as part of a Fort-to-Galle-Face walk at the day's end.

items.name: Colombo Port City & the new waterfront
items.description: A vast reclaimed district rising beside the old Fort, with a beach, marina, promenades and public art forming Colombo's newest seafront to walk in the evening breeze. It shows the city's future the way the Fort shows its past, an interesting contrast for an evening stroll before dinner.

items.name: Good Market at the Racecourse
items.description: A Saturday open-air market on the racecourse grounds gathering the island's best small makers, organic growers and street food, from artisan chocolate to handmade textiles. A relaxed, wholesome morning to browse and graze, and the easiest way to taste and take home the good things of Sri Lanka in one place.

items.name: Pettah Floating Market
items.description: A modern market built along a canal beside the Pettah railway station, its stalls set on the water for food, spices and souvenirs in a calmer, more orderly setting than the old bazaar. A gentler introduction to Pettah's trading spirit, good for a family who wants the flavour without the crush.

items.name: Ministry of Crab
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 (No. 58)
Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2021 (No. 29), long-running list member
World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 & 2023
Condé Nast Traveler Gold List 2021
items.description: Sri Lankan lagoon crab, treated like the treasure it is, in a 400-year-old Dutch hospital.

items.name: Nihonbashi
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, six consecutive years (2013–2018)
World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: Chef Dharshan Munidasa's first house, thirty years of exacting Japanese cooking with a Sri Lankan soul.

items.name: Tintagel Colombo
credentials: World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: Fine dining inside a landmark Paradise Road mansion, the city's most elegant table.

items.name: Capital Bar & Grill
credentials: World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: A polished grill room for the city's power lunches and unhurried dinners.

items.name: Yue Chuan
credentials: World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: Refined Cantonese and dim sum, held to a standard the city's Chinese rooms are measured against.

items.name: ISSO
credentials: World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: Sri Lankan prawn cookery turned into something joyful, the island's flavours, unfussy and bright.

items.name: The Verandah, Galle Face Hotel
credentials: Bar of Galle Face Hotel (Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice 2024, No. 1 Best Hotels in Asia, Rest of Asia; Best Heritage Hotel, Sri Lanka Tourism Awards 2024)
items.description: A drink on the checkerboard terrace of an 1864 colonial hotel, the Indian Ocean breaking a few feet away, the most storied sundowner in the country.

items.name: Sapphyr Lounge
credentials: Lounge bar of Shangri-La Colombo (World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Hotel 2024)
items.description: Shangri-La's lobby lounge above Galle Face, a calm, polished room for cocktails and afternoon tea over the ocean.

items.name: Capital Bar & Grill
credentials: World Culinary Awards, Sri Lanka's Best Restaurant 2024 (nominee)
items.description: A dressed-up grill room and bar for the city's unhurried dinners and late drinks, polished, contemporary, well-run.

items.name: Cloud Red
credentials: Rooftop bar of Cinnamon Grand Colombo (World Travel Awards, Sri Lanka's Leading Business Hotel 2024)
items.description: The Cinnamon Grand's rooftop bar, the city skyline and a red-lit terrace, long the address for a considered evening drink.

plan.heading: 3 days in Colombo, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Walk the Fort quarter and the restored Dutch Hospital precinct, then coffee among the arcades of the old Cargills building.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: See Geoffrey Bawa's city house at 33rd Lane by appointment, the clearest window into Sri Lanka's tropical modernism.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Ministry of Crab in the Dutch Hospital, chef Dharshan Munidasa's room for Sri Lankan lagoon crab.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Move through Pettah's bazaar streets and the Red Mosque, then the calm of Gangaramaya Temple by Beira Lake.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A private tasting of single-estate Ceylon teas, followed by an hour at the Barefoot gallery and its garden café.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners over the Indian Ocean at the Cinnamon Grand's grounds, then contemporary Sri Lankan tasting at Nihonbashi Blossom.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Early stroll along Galle Face Green as the city wakes, then breakfast of hoppers and kiribath at a quiet table.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The National Museum and the leafy Cinnamon Gardens streets, unhurried, before an afternoon spa treatment.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner at the Gallery Café, Bawa's former studio, over its courtyard and lamplight.

items.name: Fort & Galle Face
items.description: The historic core beside the sea, with the grand old hotels; suits first visits and those who want to walk to everything.

items.name: Cinnamon Gardens (Colombo 7)
items.description: The leafy, embassy-and-mansion district with the best restaurants and galleries; for quiet, style and long dinners.

items.name: Pettah
items.description: The frenetic wholesale bazaar quarter; not for basing yourself, but the most alive part of the city to spend a morning in.

events.name: Duruthu Perahera
events.note: A large temple procession at Kelaniya on the edge of Colombo, with drummers, dancers and caparisoned elephants.

events.name: Navam Perahera
events.note: Colombo's own grand full-moon procession from the Gangaramaya Temple, with dozens of elephants moving through the city by night.

events.name: Vesak
events.note: The most important Buddhist holiday; Colombo fills with lanterns and illuminated pandals, and free food stalls line the streets.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Colombo 7 (Cinnamon Gardens) for calm and space, or the Galle Face stretch for the sea; dress modestly and remove shoes and hats at temples, and note the country is officially dry on monthly poya (full-moon) days.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Land at Bandaranaike International (CMB), 32 km north of the city; a private chauffeured car handles the airport formalities and the hour's transfer, though a Cinnamon Air seaplane can lift you straight from the domestic apron to the coast if you're heading south.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Keep a private car and driver on call throughout, Colombo's traffic and heat make self-navigation pointless, and a good driver doubles as your fixer.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Buy a Dialog or Mobitel eSIM on arrival for reliable 4G/5G; hotel and lounge wifi is dependable, coverage is thin only in the deep interior.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Sri Lankan rupee (LKR); cards work in hotels and better restaurants but carry cash for smaller places and drivers, and tip 10 percent where service isn't included.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Tropical and humid year-round; December to March is the kind window (drier southwest coast, calm seas), while the southwest monsoon soaks May to September and the shorter northeast monsoon brings rain October to November.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (~4h) and Mumbai (~2h30m) on SriLankan Airlines and Air India, both with proper business cabins; IndiGo adds Delhi-Colombo nonstops from 2026 but in a single class. SriLankan's flat-bed A330 business is the pick, and its Colombo hub makes an onward hop to the Maldives or Seychelles seamless.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No mandatory vaccinations from India; keep routine jabs current and consider Hepatitis A and Typhoid. Drink bottled or filtered water only. Safe and settled for private travel post-2022, with normal city precautions; no altitude concerns.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Very easy for vegetarians and workable for Jain travellers, with a deep South Indian and Sri Lankan vegetarian tradition. Excellent Indian and pure-veg dining at Shanmugas and Green Cabin, and hotel kitchens handle Jain requests on notice.
